clue.text: Steep fine somehow overwhelms us

indicators.note: the scrambled fine swamps and so encloses the little word us
somehow says the letters of fine are put together in some new way

explanation.surface: A stiff fine seems to crush us.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Steep' looks like an adjective, as in a steep fine; it is the verb, to soak. 'somehow' gives INFE.
explanation.definitionFit: To steep tea or herbs in hot water is to soak them so their flavour is drawn out.

clue.text: Legitimate child (however naughty) comes first, it's understood

indicators.note: comes first says the child piece is placed ahead of the legitimate piece

parts.note: an imp is a naughty child
licit means lawful or legitimate

explanation.surface: A lawful child, however mischievous, takes priority, as is tacitly agreed.
explanation.definitionFit: Something implicit is implied though not stated outright.

clue.text: Ran round the Common Market like sheep

indicators.note: round says the running piece goes around the market abbreviation

parts.note: fled means ran away
EEC, the European Economic Community, was called the Common Market

explanation.surface: The European market ran round in circles like a flock of sheep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'like sheep' is a cryptic definition: shorn of their wool, and also cheated.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheep are shorn of their wool, and fleeced people are robbed or overcharged.

clue.text: Fruit in jelly a la Bristol

indicators.note: in places the fruit inside the jelly

parts.note: a shape is a jelly or blancmange set in a mould
hips are the fruit of the rose

explanation.surface: Fruit set in jelly, Bristol style.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase 'shipshape and Bristol fashion', from the port's tidy ships, makes 'a la Bristol' fair.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase shipshape and Bristol fashion means neat and orderly, in the style of the port.

clue.text: Lit by electricity or gas

parts.note: lit, as of a fire or a gun set off, means fired
amp, the unit of current, stands in for electricity

explanation.surface: Is the place lit by electricity or by gas?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lit by electricity or gas' reads as a choice of lighting; 'gas' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Methane that explodes in coal mines is the miners' name for a dangerous gas.

clue.text: Rendering a compound of nitrate and protein

indicators.note: a chemical compound combines elements, so the letters of nitrate and protein are mixed into one new arrangement

explanation.surface: A chemist renders down a compound of nitrate and protein.
explanation.definitionFit: A rendering of a piece or text is one performer's reading or translation of it.

clue.text: River rises over part, appears to break out

indicators.note: in a down clue rises means the river name is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: the Ure is a Yorkshire river

explanation.surface: A river rises over its banks and appears to break out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rises' turns URE into ERU, and 'over' places it above PT; 'appears to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A volcano or a riot that erupts bursts forth suddenly.

clue.text: Mark married? Just the opposite

parts.note: Mark Antony, the Roman general, gives his second name

explanation.surface: Was Mark married? Quite the reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: Mark Antony did marry, so 'Just the opposite' teases.
explanation.definitionFit: A word of contrary meaning is the opposite of another, such as hot for cold.

clue.text: He carries his liquor

definitions.meaning: a man who carries bags at a station or hotel
a dark, heavy beer once drunk by London market workers

explanation.definitionFit: A baggage carrier at a station, and the dark stout named after them.

clue.text: Faithful defender of many unions

parts.note: a king given the title Defender of the Faith by the Pope who married six times

explanation.definitionFit: The Tudor king was named Defender of the Faith and had six wives.

clue.text: Quietly living in Lincoln, for example

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical direction for quietly
someone living in a place is resident there

explanation.surface: Someone lives quietly in the city of Lincoln.
explanation.walkthrough: Lincoln looks like the English cathedral city; it is Abraham Lincoln.
explanation.definitionFit: Abraham Lincoln was a head of state of the United States, an example of the office.

clue.text: Put out by leaving provision store

indicators.note: leaving says the letters of the word by depart from the longer word

parts.note: a buttery is a store-room for food and drink, as in an Oxford or Cambridge college
the clue word by itself is what departs, its letters taken from either end

explanation.surface: Something gets expelled when someone quits the food store.
explanation.walkthrough: The B and Y removed are the first and last letters of the store-room word, so 'by' leaves from its two ends.
explanation.definitionFit: To utter is to emit or issue words, to give voice to them.

clue.text: It cuts the dentist's charge

parts.note: reads as a discount on a dental bill, but describes a front tooth that cuts food and is in the dentist's care

explanation.definitionFit: The front teeth that bite and slice are the cutting teeth a dentist looks after.

clue.text: Reunite disunited train

indicators.note: disunited says the letters of the word Reunite are split up and regrouped

explanation.surface: A broken-up group is brought back together.
explanation.definitionFit: A train of followers is the band of attendants that accompanies an important person.

clue.text: " Hindu god " by fashionable artist entertaining many

parts.note: in means fashionable, as in the in thing
D is 500 in Roman numerals, a large number
RA, Royal Academician, is the usual crossword artist

explanation.surface: A trendy painter puts on a show featuring a Hindu deity before a crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: D is 500 in Roman numerals, standing for 'many'; RA is a Royal Academician. Indra is the Vedic king of the gods.
explanation.definitionFit: The Vedic king of the gods wields thunder and rain in Hindu myth.

clue.text: Trying to disintegrate, meteor is

indicators.note: a meteor breaking up into pieces signals the letters of meteor is being scattered

explanation.surface: A meteor is trying to break up in the atmosphere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trying' looks like a verb, as in attempting; it is the adjective meaning wearisome.
explanation.definitionFit: Something trying is tedious and wearying, testing one's patience.

clue.text: With little rain about, everybody ends up with less water

indicators.note: about says the light rain goes around the everybody piece

parts.note: a shower is a short spell of light rain
all means everybody

explanation.surface: After only a little rain everyone finds there is less water about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ends up' is only a link between wordplay and definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A shallower pond or river has less depth of water.

clue.text: Plane is not prepared to unload

parts.note: a jet is an aeroplane

indicators.note: prepared means made ready by rearranging, so the letters of is not are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: An aircraft is not ready to be unloaded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plane' suggests a flat surface or a tool; here it is an aircraft.
explanation.definitionFit: To jettison cargo is to throw it overboard to lighten a ship or plane.

clue.text: This traitor was seen through

definitions.meaning: Roger ..., Irish nationalist hanged for treason in 1916
a hinged window frame, glass that one looks through

explanation.definitionFit: Roger Casement was executed for treason; a hinged window frame, side-opening, carries the same name.

clue.text: A suggestion Albert dropped en passant

indicators.note: dropped means the Albert piece is let fall from the suggestion

parts.note: a proposal is a suggestion
Al is short for Albert

explanation.surface: Albert let fall a passing suggestion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'en passant' is French for in passing, by the way.
explanation.definitionFit: Apropos and en passant both mean by the way, incidentally.

clue.text: Liberal MP in the drink

indicators.note: in says the MP sits inside the drink

parts.note: ale is beer, a drink

explanation.surface: A Liberal member of parliament has landed in the river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Liberal MP' reads as one politician, and 'the drink' as the sea; Liberal is the definition, and the drink is ALE.
explanation.definitionFit: Liberal helpings are generous or plentiful ones.

clue.text: Mark's part

parts.note: reads as a role or a section of a gospel, but means a fraction of the old German currency

explanation.definitionFit: The German coin worth one hundredth of a Deutschmark was its smallest unit.

clue.text: Anchorage here

parts.note: reads as a place to moor a ship, but Anchorage is the largest city of a US state

explanation.definitionFit: The city of Anchorage lies in the northernmost US state.

clue.text: She caused boatmen's deaths -see about a floral tribute

parts.note: lo, as in lo and behold, means see
re means about or concerning
a lei is a Hawaiian garland of flowers

explanation.surface: Look: a flower garland laid for those drowned by a siren.
explanation.walkthrough: The Rhine rock maiden lured boatmen to wreck on her rock with her singing.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rhine siren of German legend sang from her rock and drew boats to destruction.

clue.text: King Nebuchadnezzar's first experience

parts.note: Lear is the king in Shakespeare's tragedy

indicators.note: first means only the opening letter of the next word is taken

explanation.surface: The Babylonian king's first experience.
explanation.walkthrough: Nebuchadnezzar is a red herring king; the king wanted is LEAR, and only the N comes from Nebuchadnezzar.
explanation.definitionFit: To learn of something is to come to find it out, to undergo knowing it.

clue.text: Highest of all in the exam

indicators.note: in says the word all goes inside the exam

parts.note: a test is an exam

explanation.surface: The top mark of everyone sitting the exam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Highest of all' reads as one phrase; only 'Highest' defines, and 'all' goes in TEST.
explanation.definitionFit: The highest thing stands above all others in height, the greatest stature.

clue.text: Fish that's very good in brine

indicators.note: in places the very good piece inside the brine

parts.note: the briny is the sea
pi, short for pious, means very good in crosswords

explanation.surface: A fine fish swimming in salt water.
explanation.walkthrough: Sepia is the cuttlefish, whose ink gave the brown colour its name.
explanation.definitionFit: The cuttlefish genus is a marine mollusc loosely called a fish.

clue.text: Gulls who sink do so awkwardly

indicators.note: awkwardly says the letters of who sink do are jumbled clumsily

explanation.surface: Seabirds that dive do so in a clumsy fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gulls' looks like the seabirds; it is the verb, tricks.
explanation.definitionFit: To gull someone is to dupe or deceive them.

clue.text: Drink disarmed Arabs in them

indicators.note: disarmed means arm is taken away, so its letters leave the phrase

explanation.surface: Disarmed Arabs are found among them having a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disarmed' strips the outer letters, AR at the front and M at the back, as if lopping off limbs, leaving the drink inside the run of words.
explanation.definitionFit: A green aniseed-flavoured spirit, wormwood based, once banned in France.

clue.text: Nothing to wear in the beginning

parts.note: O is the zero, nothing
a rig is an outfit of clothing, something to wear

explanation.surface: In the beginning there was nothing to wear.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface echoes Adam and Eve in Eden.
explanation.definitionFit: The source or starting point of anything is where it began.
